subject: Persistent silence on streaming endpoint during morning traffic window — urgent coordination
messages:
From: Sam Reynolds <sam.reynolds@atlashealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, support@redwood.ai
Cc: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@atlashealth.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Live transcript stream - intermittent silence (observed today)

Hi Jonas / Redwood team,

We started seeing repeated "silent" periods on the live-transcript websocket in our production workspace this morning between 08:06 and 08:22 PT. Clients receive an open socket and then there is a multi-second gap (5-12s) with no chunked payloads; the socket remains open but the UI shows no tokens, which causes downstream UI reconnections and duplicates. The affected sessions are in cluster us-west-2.

Impact: during the 08:00-09:00 window we saw a ~5x error rate compared to baseline and a 3x latency increase for the first token. This is affecting our clinician workflow during a high-traffic shift — it's revenue impacting.

I attached a small session trace (session_trace_9981.json) with the timestamps and WebSocket-level frames. Can you confirm receipt and let us know immediate mitigations? We're open to switching to polling/non-stream fallbacks if you need us to do that while you investigate; we need an ETA for both mitigation and root cause.

Thanks,
Sam
Sam Reynolds
Head of Platform Reliability, AtlasHealth
sam.reynolds@atlashealth.com
+1 415 555 0198

Attachment: session_trace_9981.json (text/json, 78KB)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Reynolds <sam.reynolds@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 11 Jul 2027 09:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Live transcript stream - intermittent silence (observed today)

Hi Sam — thanks for the trace and the quick alert. We got it and have opened internal incident IN-9812.

Initial triage notes: the session trace shows a pattern where the TCP/WebSocket connection remains established while token frames stop arriving; HTTP chunk boundaries remain open. That aligns with a partial stall in our proxy layer under burst load rather than immediate model-side timeouts.

Immediate asks for AtlasHealth: if you can briefly switch a small subset of traffic to the non-streaming /generate endpoint (polling) that will reduce pressure on the streaming path and help confirm impact scope. If you prefer, we can perform a safe on-the-fly routing change from our side; let me know.

We will:
- Pull proxy and router metrics for the affected window (already started)
- Capture a full debug bundle and upload (redwood_debug_bundle_20270711.tar.gz)
- Start a controlled failover to a higher-throughput routing pool if needed

I'll loop in product and SRE for an early mitigation plan — I will update within 45 minutes with the first proposed mitigations. Apologies for the disruption and thank you for the clear trace.

— Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 11 Jul 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: [Action Required] IN-9812: AtlasHealth production streaming silence — mitigation plan and exec attention

Team,

Summary: AtlasHealth (customer) reported repeated multi-second gaps in chunked/WebSocket delivery during peak (08:00-09:00 PT) causing retries and duplicate downstream events. Customer is requesting an ETA and will escalate if we do not provide mitigation soon — revenue-impacting.

Observations so far (quick):
- Session traces show open WS with no token frames; chunked transfer boundaries left open for 4-12s per stall.
- Proxy ingress pipeline CPU and epoll backlog spiked in us-west-2 at 08:05:30; router queue depth increased ~6x for a short burst.
- Model layer shows normal processing times for the requests that did reach it; suggests the stall is upstream (proxy/router) or at our chunk flush scheduling path.

Immediate mitigations (proposed, will execute with SRE approval):
1) Increase routing pool capacity for AtlasHealth and move their production traffic to a higher-throughput pool (no model change) — expected near-term improvement.
2) Toggle aggressive keepalive and chunk-flush threshold to force smaller, more frequent chunk writes for affected pools (fast rollback available).
3) If 1+2 insufficient, coordinate a rolling proxy restart of the affected ingress nodes during a low-risk window (will reduce transient connections for a few minutes).

Short-term customer asks: approval to run (1) and (2) now; permission to schedule rolling restart if still degraded after 30 minutes. Also need product sign-off on a post-incident change to the chunk-flush default for high-throughput customers.

I'm escalating to Vanessa and Markus for product + SRE decisioning. Please confirm who will own the customer comms (I can handle technical updates). I attached the initial debug bundle for deep dive.

Attachments: redwood_debug_bundle_20270711.tar.gz

— Jonas

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 11 Jul 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: IN-9812 post-mitigation summary and customer ask: AtlasHealth — root cause, remediation, outreach

Team and leadership,

Summary of what we executed today (IN-9812):
- Immediately increased routing pool capacity for AtlasHealth at 09:05 PT; toggled chunk-flush threshold to more aggressive flushes at 09:08 PT. Both mitigations reduced stall frequency by ~90% for the next hour.
- Rolling restart of 4 ingress proxies began at 09:35 PT and completed by 09:42 PT during a controlled window; transient reconnects observed, but stable throughput returned.

Root cause (preliminary): a combination of (A) sudden burst of small concurrent sessions that increased epoll backlog and (B) suboptimal chunk-flush coalescing in the proxy's write path that allowed socket buffers to sit idle under contention. Under burst, chunk coalescing delayed frame emission for multiple sessions simultaneously, producing the observed multi-second gaps even though model processing was healthy.

Action items / timeline:
- Short term (next 48 hours): ship a safe proxy config change that reduces chunk-coalescing timeout for high-throughput pools (Markus owner, PR ready in 6 hours).
- Medium term (2 weeks): add backpressure monitoring and automatic per-customer pool autoscale triggers (David owner).
- Customer comms: propose a one-day service credit for the impacted window and a joint postmortem call this week. I attached a draft MAP (mutual_action_plan_AtlasHealth_Redwood.docx).

Customer impact: AtlasHealth confirmed mitigations and has asked for credit; they agreed to the rolling restart and report stable behavior following the actions.

Next: Vanessa / Markus — please confirm the PR schedule and whether we want to proactively reach out to other customers in us-west-2 with similar traffic patterns. I will prepare a short executive note for the account and draft the postmortem.

— Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
